## Excursions to the Church of Santa Prisca in Taxco

The [Church of Santa Prisca](/mexico/place/santa-prisca-taxco/) stands in the centre of [Taxco](/mexico/place/taxco/), a hillside town in Guerrero state historically associated with silver mining and metalwork. Its twin towers rise above white houses and narrow streets. The eighteenth-century church was financed by mining entrepreneur José de la Borda and is regarded as an outstanding example of Mexican Baroque architecture.

Travellers may have two different reasons to visit: to admire the architecture and sacred art, or to take part in Mass at an active Catholic church. These require different approaches to timing and the length of the stop. We offer an itinerary linking Santa Prisca with other historical and religious sites in central Mexico.

## Which excursion does Ada Tours offer?

["Cuernavaca, Taxco and Mass at Santa Prisca"](/mexico/cuernavaca/cuernavaca-taxco-pilgrimage/) is **a private excursion** with an English-speaking guide. It begins by introducing [Cuernavaca](/mexico/place/cuernavaca/), its historic buildings and cathedral, before continuing to Taxco. One Holy Mass is included in the programme, with the visit to Santa Prisca as a central element.

It is important to distinguish **an excursion to a single church** from **a multi-stop journey through two towns**. This programme includes cultural and religious stops in Cuernavaca as well as Santa Prisca. If you are interested in Taxco alone, discuss a separate format first: we do not promise a shortened version of the published route.

The excursion includes private transport, the services of an English-speaking guide, admission to the listed attractions and one Holy Mass. Specific departure times, duration and a fixed price for the separate excursion are not provided; it would be incorrect to invent any of these details.

## What to see at Santa Prisca

The experience starts on the approach to the church, where the carved façade and twin towers stand out against Taxco's tightly packed buildings. Inside, gilded wooden altarpieces, vaulting and decorations reflect the artistic traditions of New Spain. A religious service can affect the arrangements for sightseeing, so it is best to keep time for photography and detailed exploration of the interior separate from participation in Mass.

Near the church square are old streets, silver workshops and shops. They help explain how a wealthy mining town could finance such an elaborately decorated building. However, silver shopping and visits to specific workshops **are not listed as included services** on the Ada Tours excursion.

## Choosing between pilgrimage and sightseeing

| Aim | What to consider |
|---|---|
| Architecture | Time for the façade and interior |
| Catholic Mass | Confirmed service time |
| Taxco history | Walk through the town centre |
| Two towns | Route through Cuernavaca |

The pilgrimage itinerary suits those for whom attending a religious service is a goal in its own right. When choosing it, confirm the time of Mass and the sequence of the church visit. For a general introduction to the architecture, viewing the façade and interior may be enough, but that is a different arrangement and should not be presented as the ready-made excursion from the catalogue.

Santa Prisca is also included in the [seven-day religious journey through Mexico](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/). That tour covers several shrines in Mexico City and neighbouring regions, with Taxco making up just one part of the wider programme. It suits travellers wanting to bring prayer, churches and the country's history together on one journey, rather than booking separate excursions from different accommodation bases.

## Practical details before travelling

Taxco is built across steep hillsides, so even a walk around the historic centre can involve slopes and uneven cobblestones. Comfortable footwear is important for visiting the church, and clothing should be appropriate for an active religious site. If anyone has mobility restrictions, mention them when arranging the itinerary and stops.

Before booking, confirm the starting point of the excursion, departure time, availability of interior visits and arrangements for Mass. Religious services and visits to historic churches may depend on the parish's current schedule; unrestricted access on every date cannot be promised.

## Frequently asked questions about Santa Prisca excursions

### Can I see the church on an excursion from Cuernavaca?

Yes. We offer an [itinerary through Cuernavaca and Taxco](/mexico/cuernavaca/cuernavaca-taxco-pilgrimage/) that includes Santa Prisca in the overall programme.

### Is Mass included on the pilgrimage excursion?

Yes. One Holy Mass is included in this excursion. Confirm the exact service time for your chosen date.

### Is an English-speaking guide included?

Yes. Our private excursion includes an English-speaking guide.

### Is there a separate fixed price for visiting the church?

We do not quote a fixed price for this itinerary. Its terms need to be considered in relation to the entire excursion, not to entering the church independently.

## Excursions to Santo Domingo Church in Mexico City

[Santo Domingo Church](/mexico/place/santo-domingo-mexico-city/) stands in Mexico City's historic centre. Its reddish stone façade and Baroque decoration recall the Dominican monastery that once occupied a large part of the neighbourhood. The present church dates mainly to the eighteenth century; nearby buildings help visitors imagine how this district of New Spain's capital developed.

You can visit Santo Domingo for a quiet introduction to its architecture or include it in a religious programme with Mass. Ada Tours offers the latter as part of a historic-centre excursion and a longer pilgrimage tour.

## An excursion with Mass through central Mexico City

["Mexico City Churches, Mass and Garibaldi Square"](/mexico/santo-domingo-mexico-city/mexico-city-pilgrimage-garibaldi/) is **a private excursion with an English-speaking guide**. The programme begins in the historic centre, visiting [Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/) and Santo Domingo Church, where Holy Mass is scheduled. It then continues to [Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/), the National Palace and historic palatial buildings before finishing at [Garibaldi Square](/mexico/place/garibaldi-plaza/) with an introduction to mariachi music.

This sequence reveals how religious monuments, government history and living urban culture share the same district. However, admission to every building cannot be assumed on every date. In particular, **entry to the National Palace** depends on official events and current access arrangements; we explain these restrictions in advance.

The excursion includes private transport, an English-speaking guide, admission tickets to the listed attractions and one Holy Mass. No fixed price is published for this standalone excursion, and the balance between exterior and interior visits needs to be confirmed in light of current restrictions.

## What to see inside and around Santo Domingo

The church is associated with the Dominican order, which established a presence in the capital soon after the Spanish conquest. Its interior preserves Baroque altarpieces, side chapels and religious images. Among the venerated images are Our Lady of the Rosary and Our Lady of Covadonga. Take time to see these details when no service is being disturbed.

Santo Domingo Square lies in front of the church. To its south is a neighbourhood of historic buildings and former administrative complexes. The area is close to Zócalo, allowing an excursion to include several neighbouring sites in the centre without travelling to another city. Nevertheless, traffic, access restrictions and service times affect the actual order of stops.

The name **Santo Domingo** also appears in other Mexican cities. This itinerary refers specifically to the church in the capital. The Dominican church and Chapel of the Rosary in Puebla are different historic sites and should not be confused with this route.

## Which format should you choose?

| Format | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Church and neighbourhood | Architecture and the square |
| Ada Tours excursion | Mass and central Mexico City |
| Pilgrimage tour | Several cities |

If your priority is photographing the façade and walking through historic streets, read our [guide to the church itself](/mexico/place/santo-domingo-mexico-city/). If you want to see religious sites and then discover different sides of the capital, choose the [Mass and Garibaldi excursion](/mexico/santo-domingo-mexico-city/mexico-city-pilgrimage-garibaldi/). For several days of religious activities, we offer a [seven-day journey through Mexico](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/), with Santo Domingo as one stop on the pilgrimage.

Pay attention to service times when choosing a day. Tourist visits may be restricted during church events. Comfortable shoes are useful for walking through the historic centre, where the route involves squares, stone pavements and pedestrian crossings.

## Frequently asked questions about Santo Domingo in Mexico City

### Is Mass included in the Ada Tours excursion?

Yes. One Holy Mass is scheduled as part of the published pilgrimage excursion. The specific date and time must be arranged in advance.

### Can I combine the church with Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral?

Yes. Both are included in the [historic-centre excursion](/mexico/santo-domingo-mexico-city/mexico-city-pilgrimage-garibaldi/), along with Zócalo and other landmarks.

### Is entry to the National Palace guaranteed?

No. The itinerary explicitly states that access depends on government events and the building's operating conditions. This restriction also applies to a private excursion.

### In what language is the excursion conducted?

Ada Tours lists English as the guiding language. Another language must not be assumed to be included without separate agreement.

## Mexico City churches, Mass at Santo Domingo and Garibaldi Square

Mexico City's historic centre brings together Catholic churches, public squares and palaces associated with the capital's development. Our excursion passes through [Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/), [Santo Domingo Church](/mexico/place/santo-domingo-mexico-city/) and the [Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/), ending with an introduction to local musical culture at [Garibaldi Square](/mexico/place/garibaldi-plaza/).

This is **a private excursion with an English-speaking guide and transport**. One Holy Mass and admission to the listed attractions are included. The total duration is not specified, so the sequence of visits depends on the service schedule and access restrictions at official buildings.

## Zócalo and Santo Domingo Church

In the morning, the route leads to the city's main square, **Zócalo**. Some of Mexico City's most important monuments stand here, including the cathedral and National Palace. The neighbourhood is an excellent introduction to the city's history, with colonial architecture beside the public spaces of the modern capital.

**Holy Mass** is celebrated at [Santo Domingo Church](/mexico/place/santo-domingo-mexico-city/). The church is associated with devotion to Our Lady of the Rosary and Our Lady of Covadonga. Observe the rules for conduct and photography when visiting: this is an active place of worship where religious services continue.

For pilgrims, Mass is a meaningful part of the day in its own right. For travellers interested in urban history, the visit introduces the religious culture of colonial Mexico City.

## The Metropolitan Cathedral and historic palaces

The next stop is [Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/) beside the main square. Its architecture and interior decoration reflect centuries of development in Mexican art.

The itinerary also includes the [National Palace](/mexico/place/national-palace-mexico-city/) and the [Old Archbishop's Palace](/mexico/place/old-archbishop-palace/), associated with Juan de Zumárraga.

**Entry to the National Palace depends on government events and official access conditions.** It is an active government building, so visits to the interior, including its historic murals, may be restricted or unavailable on some days. We therefore cannot guarantee entry on every date.

## Garibaldi Square and mariachi music

After the churches and palaces, the route continues to [Garibaldi Square](/mexico/place/garibaldi-plaza/), a place closely associated with mariachi music. Ensembles performing traditional Mexican songs can be heard here.

Moving from the solemn atmosphere of the churches to this musical square reveals different sides of Mexico City's cultural life. We introduce you to the location, but **a particular concert, performance duration or private booking of musicians is not advertised**.

## How the private excursion is organised

We provide private transport, an English-speaking guide, admission to the listed attractions and one Mass. A specific starting time, price and included meals are not listed separately. When choosing a date, consider the religious-service schedule, church opening hours and the National Palace's operating arrangements.

The itinerary includes several historic sites, so comfortable footwear and clothing appropriate for active churches are useful. Explore more cultural destinations in our [Culture and History section](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about this Mexico City excursion

### At which church is Mass celebrated?

The itinerary specifies **Santo Domingo Church in Mexico City**.

### Is transport included?

Yes. The excursion provides **private transport and an English-speaking guide**.

### Can we see the murals in the National Palace?

Entry depends on official access arrangements. Visiting the rooms and murals **is not guaranteed**, particularly during government events.

### Is a mariachi performance in Garibaldi included?

The itinerary includes a visit to the square, which is known for its musicians. **A separate concert is not listed as an included service**.

### How long does the excursion last?

The published description does not specify an exact duration; this is agreed when arranging the day's programme.

## Tours featuring Mexico City churches, Mass and Garibaldi Square

Religious shrines, colonial architecture and Mexican musical traditions are best appreciated on a journey that devotes a full day to the historic centre. The ["Mexico City Churches, Mass and Garibaldi Square" excursion](/mexico/santo-domingo-mexico-city/mexico-city-pilgrimage-garibaldi/) is part of the [seven-day religious journey through Mexico](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/). It is scheduled for **3 April 2027**, day three of the trip.

This page helps you choose **a multi-day tour that includes this excursion**, rather than an independent walk through Mexico City. We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring the excursion module. Similar stops or the general description "capital city tour" do not mean that another itinerary includes Mass at Santo Domingo Church specifically.

## Why the historic centre deserves a full day

On the [religious journey through Mexico](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/), the first days focus on the capital's spiritual and historic heritage. After arrival and the visit to the Shrine of Our Lady of Guadalupe, the itinerary moves to Mexico City's old squares and cathedrals before continuing on excursions across central Mexico.

On day three, you head to [Zócalo](/mexico/place/mexico-city-zocalo/), the capital's main square, and attend Mass at [Santo Domingo Church](/mexico/place/santo-domingo-mexico-city/). The programme then includes [Mexico City Metropolitan Cathedral](/mexico/place/mexico-city-metropolitan-cathedral/), the [National Palace](/mexico/place/national-palace-mexico-city/) and the Old Archbishop's Palace. It ends at [Garibaldi Square](/mexico/place/garibaldi-plaza/), known for its mariachi musicians.

These are two different experiences within one excursion. The churches and buildings around Zócalo introduce the city's history and Catholic traditions, while Garibaldi reveals its living musical culture. The square is on the northwestern edge of the historic centre, where mariachi musicians perform in different groups and offer their own shows. Hearing mariachi in the square should not be confused with a separately paid private musical programme: none is listed as part of this excursion.

## How the excursion fits into the pilgrimage week

| Stage of the trip | Main focus |
|---|---|
| 2 April | Basilica of Guadalupe and Anthropology Museum |
| 3 April | Santo Domingo, Mexico City cathedrals, Garibaldi |
| 4 April | Tlaxcala, Ocotlán and Puebla |
| 5 April | Cuernavaca and Taxco |
| 6 April | Teotihuacán, Tulpetlac, Tlatelolco |

The group stays overnight in Mexico City throughout the week. The package includes **six nights** at Casa Blanca 4-star hotel or equivalent, private transfers, an English-speaking guide and scheduled breakfasts and dinners. There are **five Holy Masses** over the seven days. The itinerary therefore primarily suits travellers who wish to visit Catholic shrines in central Mexico while keeping the religious programme integrated into the overall journey.

If archaeology without a series of Masses is your main interest, compare [Mexico's cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/mexico/) and the specific inclusions of each. Many trips visit the historic centre, but the excursion module combining Santo Domingo and Garibaldi must be checked separately.

## Details to confirm before choosing the tour

**Access to the National Palace is conditional.** This remains an active government building, so visits to its interiors, including historic murals, depend on official arrangements and events. The programme explicitly warns that entry may be restricted or unavailable. Choosing an entire pilgrimage solely to see the palace interiors would therefore be unwise.

**Mass must be coordinated with the actual schedule.** The tour provides religious services as part of its programme. Church visiting times and the order of excursions depend on religious events and operational arrangements. A standalone excursion and a multi-day tour may have different guiding conditions; consult each product's page.

**This itinerary consists of day trips from Mexico City.** After the excursions, the group returns to the same hotel rather than moving to a new city every night. This suits travellers who value stable accommodation and a single base. However, the days covering Tlaxcala, Puebla, Cuernavaca and Taxco involve road journeys, so consider the overall pace beforehand.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with Mexico City churches and Garibaldi

### On which day does the excursion take place?

On the [seven-day religious journey](/mexico/tour/mexico-religious-journey/), it is scheduled for **3 April 2027**, day three.

### Is Holy Mass at Santo Domingo included?

Yes. Mass at [Santo Domingo Church](/mexico/place/santo-domingo-mexico-city/) is part of this excursion module and one of the pilgrimage programme's five Masses.

### Is entry to the National Palace guaranteed?

No. The [National Palace](/mexico/place/national-palace-mexico-city/) remains a government building, and official events may restrict access. The excursion description explicitly notes this condition.

### Can I book the separate excursion without the full week?

Yes. The [standalone excursion page](/mexico/santo-domingo-mexico-city/mexico-city-pilgrimage-garibaldi/) describes its own route and conditions. This catalogue specifically covers multi-day tours that include the module.

## Excursions in Taxco: the silver town, Santa Prisca and the route via Cuernavaca

[Taxco](/mexico/place/taxco/) is set among the hills of Guerrero state. White façades, red-tiled roofs and narrow streets make it a distinctive colonial town, but the main attraction is its combination of architecture, religious history and silversmithing. The Church of Santa Prisca stands at the centre, surrounded by jewellery shops and workshops near Zócalo Square.

We offer the [private "Cuernavaca, Taxco and Mass at Santa Prisca" excursion](/mexico/cuernavaca/cuernavaca-taxco-pilgrimage/). It covers several stops: first the Palace of Cortés and cathedral in Cuernavaca, then Taxco and the Church of Santa Prisca. The excursion includes **private transport, an English-speaking guide, admission to the listed attractions and one Holy Mass**. Shopping for silver and a separate jewellery-making workshop are not included.

## What makes Taxco different from Mexico's other historic cities?

Taxco has been associated with silver mining and metalwork for centuries. This tradition is visible in shop windows, markets and small workshops. Jewellery differs in design, fineness, technique and origin. If buying a piece is important to you, allow time to compare items, ask for documentation of the metal's characteristics and remember that shopping is not a substitute for a cultural excursion.

Central Taxco's streets run up steep hills. The scenery is beautiful, but walking requires more effort than in a flat historic city centre. Cobbled slopes and steps matter especially when travelling with young children, older visitors or people with limited mobility.

The **Church of Santa Prisca and San Sebastián** stands out for its carved stone ornament and twin towers. It is a notable example of eighteenth-century Mexican Baroque architecture. The square offers an opportunity to study the façade, while viewpoints higher in town reveal the church's commanding position in Taxco's skyline. Access to the interior depends on current opening conditions and religious events.

## A journey with Mass: the purpose of the Ada Tours itinerary

We arrange this as **a cultural and religious journey**, not a shopping tour. It begins in Cuernavaca with the Palace of Cortés and the cathedral, before continuing to hillside Taxco, where Mass is scheduled at Santa Prisca.

This combination suits travellers who want to see different periods of Mexico's Christian heritage: Cuernavaca's early colonial history and Taxco's ornate Baroque architecture. Visiting active religious buildings and taking part in Mass calls for appropriate conduct and respect for worshippers.

If your priority is **jewellery workshops**, that is a different request. Taxco is certainly known for its silver products, but the confirmed Ada Tours excursion does not promise a visit to a particular workshop, a meeting with a silversmith or silver at a special price. Such activities can be discussed separately once their inclusion is confirmed.

## Planning the road journey and time in town

Taxco lies south of Mexico City. When planning the itinerary, allow for traffic leaving the capital and the fact that the town centre sits on steep streets. A route combining Cuernavaca and Taxco requires time for travel between the towns as well as sightseeing.

Duration, departure time and an individual price are not specified for this excursion. They cannot be inferred from the town's popularity or the duration of similar tourist products. When arranging the journey, agree the departure time, the length of each stop and the amount of walking suitable for the group.

For independent exploration of the town and its culture, see our [Taxco guide](/mexico/place/taxco/). To compare historical and religious itineraries across other regions, explore the general ["Culture and History" catalogue](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Preparing for your visit

- **Walking:** wear non-slip shoes, bring water and allow time for stairs and steep slopes.
- **Worship:** confirm service times in advance, dress respectfully and follow church rules.
- **Silver shopping:** set your own budget and check the quality of the items; purchases are not part of the published excursion package.
- **Photography:** daylight shows off the tiled roofs and sculptural church decoration, but interior entry and photography may be restricted locally.

If your trip coincides with a major local festival, opening hours and movement around the centre may differ from normal. Check the official event calendar and access to individual sites for the actual date rather than assuming attendance at processions is automatically included.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions in Taxco

### Does Ada Tours offer a separate tour of silver workshops only?

The confirmed Taxco catalogue offers a private excursion via Cuernavaca with a visit to Santa Prisca and Mass. A separate silver-making workshop is not advertised as part of it.

### What is included on the excursion via Cuernavaca?

According to the description, it includes private transport, an English-speaking guide, admission tickets to the listed sites and one Mass. See the [excursion programme](/mexico/cuernavaca/cuernavaca-taxco-pilgrimage/) for its terms and inclusions.

### Can I see Santa Prisca without attending Mass?

The church is a famous Taxco landmark, but the current Ada Tours product includes Mass. Changing the religious part of the excursion or arranging sightseeing at another time requires separate agreement.

### Is Taxco suitable for a leisurely walk?

Yes, provided you allow enough time for stops and take its steep cobbled streets into account. Discuss the length of walking sections in advance if slopes are difficult for anyone in the group.
